en: The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an 8.2-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Boracay Island's famous white sand is actually composed of crushed coral and microscopic shells called foraminifera.
Lake Danao in Leyte is shaped exactly like a guitar and sits at an elevation of 600 meters.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has eyes that are actually as large as its entire brain.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo released so much ash that it lowered global average temperatures by half a degree.
Bohol's Chocolate Hills consist of over 1,200 perfectly cone-shaped mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Palawan is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching over 400 kilometers between the South China Sea and Sulu Sea.
The Philippine Sea contains the Philippine Trench, which plunges to a depth of over 10,500 meters below sea level.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines at 2,954 meters and shelters the rare Philippine eagle.
The Philippines is an archipelago consisting of 7,641 islands, which is 534 more than the old count of 7,107.
The Rafflesia, the world's largest individual flower, blooms in Philippine rainforests and can grow up to one meter wide.
Baguio City's average year-round temperature is 18 degrees Celsius because it sits at a high elevation of 1,500 meters.
